title: Candor — attested authorization protocol for irreversible actions (v1)
description: Candor v1 is a thin protocol for human authorization of irreversible actions (DOI minting, git push). The human authorizes with one command using a git-style short digest of the subject plus a reason; the intent (subject-digest, action, target, reason, actor, UTC) is recorded as an in-toto Statement v1 and OpenTimestamps-attested, so the authorization itself is non-repudiable. It reuses in-toto (envelope) and OpenTimestamps (notarisation); the only new element is the candor/v1 predicate profile and the rule that the raw .ots is never stored, only its AyeSHA encoding. Motivated by the 'no donkey work for humans' contract: sufficient intent is a single command plus a short signed-off character string.
notes: Predicate type https://project-ilm.org/attestations/candor/v1. Reference implementation: attest/candor.sh in project-ilm/tok-doi. Model of record: Claude Opus 4.8.
